Federal Reserve Board announces approval of application by First Midwest Bancorp

Published 2026-10-07 06:30 UTC

The Federal Reserve Board on Wednesday announced its approval of the application by First Midwest Bancorp, Inc., Springfield, Illinois, to acquire Prairie State Bank and Trust, Decatur, Illinois, and thereby indirectly acquire its subsidiary state member bank.

In evaluating the application, the Board considered the competitive effects of the proposal in the relevant banking markets, the financial and managerial resources of the companies involved, the convenience and needs of the communities to be served, and the records of the insured depository institutions under the Community Reinvestment Act. The Board also considered the effectiveness of the companies in combating money laundering and the extent to which the proposal would result in greater or more concentrated risks to the stability of the United States banking or financial system.

The Board found that the acquisition would not significantly increase concentration in any relevant banking market. After the transaction, the combined organization would control less than 15 percent of deposits in each of the local markets where both banks operate. The Board received two public comments on the proposal, which it considered along with information provided by the applicant.

The approval is conditioned on the applicant's compliance with all commitments made in connection with the application, including commitments to maintain branch services in rural communities currently served by the target bank for at least three years. The transaction may not be completed before the fifteenth calendar day after the effective date of the order, and must be completed within three months unless the period is extended.

The Board's order, along with the votes of the Board members, is attached. The Board acts on applications under the Bank Holding Company Act and the Federal Reserve Act, and publishes its orders so that the public can see the factors it considered.

For media inquiries, please email the Board's public affairs office or call during business hours. Copies of the application and public comments are available from the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago upon request.
